decisions.title: Freshness and exact timestamps
decisions.context: Chris0Jeky/developer-lens::HUMAN_TODO.md::q-6 asks whether to show exact retrieval time, hour-rounded, day-rounded or age-only.
decisions.recommendation: Default UI to age/coarse status, expose exact local timestamp in an inspection drawer, and keep public/exported projections at day/week grain or suppress entirely.

options.label: Coarse default, exact local detail
options.description: Useful for debugging without making operational timestamps primary or exportable.

options.label: Exact everywhere
options.description: Maximum traceability but noisier and less privacy-preserving.

options.label: Age-only everywhere
options.description: Clean and private, but weak for diagnosing collection freshness.

decisions.title: Telemetry
decisions.context: No remote telemetry provider or privacy notice is selected, and current local diagnostics are sufficient for a solo project.
decisions.recommendation: Keep remote telemetry disabled. Add structured local diagnostics and an explicit user-generated support bundle first.

options.label: Local diagnostics only
options.description: Matches local-first posture and avoids a premature policy/vendor decision.

options.label: Select remote telemetry now
options.description: Could aid debugging, but adds a new sink before distribution warrants it.

decisions.title: Distribution ladder
decisions.context: The roadmap proposes source run, Lab uvx/PyPI, gh launcher, npm CLI and desktop shell.
decisions.recommendation: After v0.2 value: make source-run excellent, ship a thin npm CLI and gh launcher, then measure setup friction before an Electron shell.

options.label: CLI → gh → desktop
options.description: Tests demand and packaging boundaries incrementally.

options.label: Desktop first
options.description: Best casual UX, but highest signing/update/security cost.

options.label: Source-run only
options.description: Low maintenance, but caps adoption and portfolio legibility.

decisions.title: Team mode boundary
decisions.context: The constitution authorizes aggregate team/workstream/system views but not individual leaderboards.
decisions.recommendation: Keep Team mode aggregate-only with explicit audience, coverage and uncertainty. Treat every individual comparison as a separate owner/consent/research gate.

options.label: Aggregate system/team mode
options.description: Useful for engineering direction without turning the product into surveillance.

options.label: Add individual ranking
options.description: Commercially tempting but conflicts with current mandate and evidence posture.

decisions.title: Taskdeck integration identity
decisions.context: Chris0Jeky/developer-lens::HUMAN_TODO.md::q-6 leaves the exact immutable Taskdeck ref and activation card unresolved.
decisions.recommendation: Pin an exact Taskdeck commit/schema in a local private integration config; keep public docs at compatibility-range level and require an activation card for writes.

options.label: Exact local pin + public compatibility range
options.description: Reproducible without leaking machine/integration state into public planning.

options.label: Track Taskdeck main
options.description: Simple but non-reproducible and prone to silent import drift.

decisions.title: First real canary scope
decisions.context: The owner already selected one public repository for a bounded metadata-only github.core proof, but no real collection should run before readiness exits.
decisions.recommendation: Use exactly one owner-selected public repository, metadata-only, tiny request budget, no prose/person fields, short retention, explicit delete/replay drill, and no public derived output.

options.label: One bounded public metadata canary
options.description: Maximizes learning per unit of new trust surface.

options.label: Start with several repositories
options.description: More representative, but obscures failures and multiplies identity/deletion scope.

options.label: Start with private repositories
options.description: High-value data, but needlessly raises stakes for the first activation.
